About us

The External Reporting Board (XRB) is an independent Crown entity under the Crown Entities Act 2004. We develop and issue financial reporting, auditing and assurance, and climate standards for for-profit, not-for-profit and public sector entities in New Zealand. For more information about the XRB go to https://www.xrb.govt.nz

    Heard of He Tauira? 👀 Over the next few weeks we will be posting a series of explainer videos on He Tauira and the underlying concepts. In our first video Joe Hanita, Chair of the Kaitiaki Group that oversaw its development, introduces us to the what and why of He Tauira. In a nutshell, He Tauira is a voluntary conceptual reporting framework specifically designed to guide reporting entities in Aotearoa New Zealand to consider how they articulate their intergenerational impact for people and planet. 🔗 To access He Tauira, implementation resources and other videos in our explainer series, visit: https://lnkd.in/eHRSMjX2 If you would like to connect with the growing community of practitioners, email us at sustainability@xrb.govt.nz

    ⏰ Two weeks to go: NZ CS 1 amendment consultation closes soon There are just two weeks left to provide feedback on the XRB’s proposed amendments to NZ CS 1 Climate-related Disclosures, focused on GHG emissions. The proposals aim to: 📗 Better align NZ CS 1 with international requirements, including recent IFRS S2 and AASB S2 amendments 📗 Permit exclusion of certain financial activity emissions from scope 3 (while still requiring transparent disclosure) 📗 Embed existing guidance on excluding emissions sources into the standard We encourage all interested stakeholders to have their say. If you are a climate reporting entity, user of climate statements, or involved in emissions measurement, this is your opportunity to shape the final requirements. 👉 Read our consultation material and complete the online survey: https://lnkd.in/emhg3_d5 🗓️ Submissions close 5pm, 29 July 2026

    The first academic research paper examining He Tauira has arrived and it has sparked discussion within the Accounting and Finance Association of Australia and New Zealand (AFAANZ) Indigenous Perspectives on Accounting Special Interest Group.   Congratulations to Ellie Norris and 'Iki Uele for the publication of their research paper, and to Nives Botica Redmayne and Yinka Moses for helping them bring the panel session to life. We look forward to supporting the growth of He Tauira in practice and academia, and sharing insights with our community as we witness the evolution of reporting.   Dive into the finding and practical implications here https://lnkd.in/epTxUKBf Find the He Tauira framework and our new video series here https://lnkd.in/eHRSMjX2

    Ellie Norris
    1w Edited

    🤩 Indigenous Perspectives on Accounting SIG 🤩 It was a great pleasure today to discuss He Tauira, a new voluntary conceptual framework from the External Reporting Board, with colleagues at the Accounting and Finance Association of Australia and New Zealand (AFAANZ) Indigenous Perspectives Special Interest Group. This important framework brings te ao Māori into conversations about strategic planning and performance measurement, and I hope it can help reshape how we practise and teach accounting to capture intergenerational, cultural, environmental and social value (and much more!). I was privileged to sit alongside aku hoamahi Nives Botica Redmayne, Yinka Moses, and 'Iki Uele for this discussion. This conversation forms part of a broader research workstream that I hope we can continue to develop. Iki and I recently published this paper https://lnkd.in/eJq7bcgJ in Meditari Accountancy Research that connects closely with He Tauira, and I am excited to continue this important mahi alongside these wonderful colleagues. Our sincere thanks and appreciation go to Professor Kerry Bodle and CPA Australia (Holly M., Adam Suess, Rebecca Keppel-Jones) for creating the space for us to share this work, and for their ongoing support of the kaupapa. For more details of He Tauira, check out https://lnkd.in/eMgkXhvw Rikki Owen, Judy Ryan, Amelia Sharman, Joe Hanita, Sheree Ryan and many others... we hope we did justice to your incredible work! #HeTauira #IndigenousAccounting #TeAoMāori #AFAANZ #CPAAustralia #XRB #AccountingResearch #SustainabilityReporting #UniversityOfCanterbury

    📢 Consultation now open: proposed amendments to NZ CS 1 The XRB has released a targeted consultation on proposed amendments to NZ CS 1 Climate-related Disclosures, focused on GHG emissions. The proposals respond to stakeholder feedback and aim to better align New Zealand requirements with recent international developments, including IFRS S2 and AASB S2. Key proposals include: 🏭 Permitting the exclusion of certain financial activity emissions (e.g. derivatives, underwriting, capital markets) from scope 3 disclosures 🏭 Incorporating existing XRB staff guidance on excluding emissions sources into the standard These changes are intended to reduce cost and complexity, while maintaining transparency through required disclosure of exclusions. 📅 Consultation closes 29 July 2026 We encourage all interested stakeholders to review the proposals and provide feedback via the online survey: https://lnkd.in/emhg3_d5 There is also a walk-through webcast which outlines our proposals: https://lnkd.in/eVD8FpJ2

    As an early adopter of He Tauira, Whānau Āwhina Plunket is using the framework to strengthen its focus on what really matters. That clearer focus has helped Plunket develop a new strategy that connects purpose, strategy and long-term impact, and sets a pathway to reporting on the outcomes that it is seeking to achieve.   Rather than starting with metrics or outputs, this work begins with clarity about what matters most. For Plunket, that has created a stronger foundation for understanding, articulating and reporting the outcomes it is working towards and the longer-term impacts it wants to have.   Louise Eunson, GM Corporate Services, shares what this looks like in practice: “He Tauira has helped us bring together our ‘why’ much more clearly, particularly in how we connect purpose, vision and long-term impact. It gave us a framework for how we think about and articulate the intergenerational impact we want to have for whānau of today, and whānau of the future.”   “He Tauira gave us a way to tangibly weave our many sustainability considerations into our strategy rather than them being add-ons.” It’s a powerful example of what early adoption of He Tauira can look like in practice. We’re grateful to be working alongside Whānau Āwhina Plunket as they continue using He Tauira.   For more on the He Tauira framework, visit the XRB website: https://lnkd.in/eHRSMjX2 If you are interested in becoming an early adopter contact: sustainability@xrb.govt.nz To read more about Plunket’s new strategy, visit the Plunket website: https://lnkd.in/euRi7EGQ #HeTauira #SustainabilityReporting #PurposeDriven #IntegratedThinking

    We’re proud to share the launch of our new five-year strategy - Kotahitanga. Grounded in unity and togetherness, it reflects how we’ll continue to work alongside whānau across Aotearoa to support the wellbeing of pēpi, tamariki, and their communities. Our vision is strong communities, confident whānau, thriving tamariki. Our purpose is to walk alongside whānau in their communities to support the growth, development and wellbeing of tamariki under five. Some our Plunket whānau share what Kotahitanga means to them - and why they show up every day for pēpi and tamariki across the motu. We’re excited about what’s ahead, and the difference our goals and commitments in Kotahitanga: Our Strategy 2026–2031 will make for whānau.
